Pakistan's Ruling Party Leads PoK Election Amid Boycott Calls

Candidates backed by Pakistan Muslim League-N (PML-N), the party of former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, have secured 24 out of 34 seats in the first two phases of voting in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (PoK). The election proceeded despite a boycott call from a banned group. At least one newly elected legislator, Rukhsar Ahmed, is reportedly out on police bail in the UK in connection with child sex offense allegations from the 1990s. A UK judge permitted him to travel to Pakistan for campaigning.
